// eras.mjs — THE FIVE (operator, value) PAIRS THE ERA TABLE READS THROUGH A
// TABLE AND NO RULE NAMES.
//
// `attr_needs` in facts/js-env.rofl carries `**`, `??`, `??=`, `||=` and `&&=`;
// `rules/js-env.rofl` reads them as `attr_needs(L, K, Key, V, F),
// ast_attr[code](N, Key, V)`, so both arguments of the `ast_attr` literal are
// VARIABLES and `attr_key_read` — which sees a rule NAMING a key — cannot see
// the read at all.
//
// WITHOUT A SITE THE HOLE IS UNFALSIFIABLE. The js-call corpus carries thirteen
// operator values and not one of these five, so `unconsumed_value[audit]` was
// green over a gap it would have reported the moment somebody wrote `a ** b` in
// a fixture. This file is that site: with the bridge in rules/js-attrs.rofl the
// audit stays empty, and without it these five values are reported as read by
// nobody while the era layer gates three features on them.
//
// EVERY OTHER OPERATOR HERE IS ALREADY EXCUSED BY NAME (`+`), deliberately: a
// fixture that also introduced an unexcused value would make the mutant's
// answer a mixture rather than exactly the five.
export function eras(a, b) {
  const power = a ** b;
  let near = a ?? b;
  near ??= b;
  let some = a;
  some ||= b;
  let both = b;
  both &&= a;
  return power + near + some + both;
}
